title: Elliptic left parametrix as an identity on distributions
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth Riemannian metric and its positive volume form. Let $B,C$ be smooth real vector bundles of the same finite rank with smooth positive definite fibre metrics. Let $d\geq1$ be an integer and let $P:\Gamma^\infty(B)\to\Gamma^\infty(C)$ be a real-linear differential operator locally given in smooth frames by $P=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq d}a_\alpha(x)\partial^\alpha$, with smooth coefficients, such that $\sum_{|\alpha|=d}a_\alpha(x)\xi^\alpha:B_x\to C_x$ is invertible for every nonzero real covector $\xi$. Extend $P$ to distributions by that local formula using derivatives defined by duality. With $\mathcal D'$ and $\Psi^r$ as in [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators], there exist $A\in\Psi^{-d}(C,B)$ and a real smooth kernel $K(x,y)\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf R}(B_y,B_x)$ such that $$A(Pu)=u+R_Ku\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal D'(B).$$ Here $R_K$ is the distributional integral operator with kernel $K$ and the fixed volume form. The equality is in $\mathcal D'(B)$ and requires no Sobolev regularity of $u$.

source.place: Part I section 3.B, construction following Definition 3.8, printed pp.13–14 (PDF pages 25–26); real bundle version of the symbol inverse and smoothing remainder; WANTED locally, read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/hodge-ams.pdf

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-pseudodifferential-leading-calculus](iii) with $k=d$: the distributional $P$ has order $d$ and global homogeneous leading symbol $p_d=i^d\sum_{|\alpha|=d}a_\alpha\xi^\alpha$. The hypothesis makes $p_d$ invertible away from zero. Put $b=p_d^{-1}:C_{\mathbf C,x}\to B_{\mathbf C,x}$. In real frames the adjugate-over-determinant formula shows that $b$ is smooth; $b(x,t\xi)=t^{-d}b(x,\xi)$ for $t>0$. Also $p_d(x,-\xi)=\overline{p_d(x,\xi)}$, so the same reality identity holds for $b$. To check the symbol estimates after a cutoff, each $\partial_x^\alpha\partial_\xi^\beta b$ is homogeneous of degree $-d-|\beta|$ and bounded on each compact chart set times the unit sphere; the cutoff region is compact in frequency. Thus $b$ satisfies the hypotheses of (i). Obtain a real $A_0\in\Psi^{-d}(C,B)$ with leading symbol $b$. By (ii) and (iii), $A_0P$ and $I_B$ have order zero and the same leading symbol $bp_d=\operatorname{id}_{B_{\mathbf C}}$, whence $$E:=A_0P-I_B\in\Psi^{-1}(B,B).$$ Use the current [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators] on the strong distributional dual: each local term is $L=\chi\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(a)\psi$ and $(Lu)(\phi)=u(L^t\phi)$, with both spatial cutoffs included. The input cutoff keeps $L^t\phi$ compactly supported. Clause (iii) identifies the differential-operator action with the local derivative-by-duality extension required here.

source.place: §3.B, paragraph following Definition 3.8, printed p.13: truncate the inverse symbol and compose

proof.text: Let $T_0=I_B$ and $T_j=(-E)^j$ for $j\geq1$. The order rules of [lem-sfb-pseudodifferential-leading-calculus](ii) give $T_j\in\Psi^{-j}(B,B)$ by induction: $T_0$ has order zero and $T_{j+1}=(-E)T_j$ has order at most $-1-j$. Apply [lem-sfb-pseudodifferential-asymptotic-sum] with $r=0$ and $E=F=B$ to obtain one real $Q\in\Psi^0(B,B)$ such that, for every $L\geq1$, $$Q-S_L\in\Psi^{-L}(B,B),\qquad S_L=\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}(-E)^j.$$ This is an asymptotic realization, requiring no norm-smallness of $E$ or convergence of its geometric series.

source.place: §3.B, paragraph following Definition 3.8, printed pp.13–14: asymptotic geometric expansion

proof.text: Set $A=QA_0\in\Psi^{-d}(C,B)$ by [lem-sfb-pseudodifferential-leading-calculus](ii). For each $L\geq1$, cancellation of the finite sums gives $$S_L(I_B+E)-I_B=(-1)^{L-1}E^L.$$ Since $A_0P=I_B+E$, associativity and distributivity of composition on distributions give $$AP-I_B=(Q-S_L)(I_B+E)+(-1)^{L-1}E^L.$$ The first term has order at most $-L+0=-L$, because $I_B+E\in\Psi^0$; the second has order at most $-L$ by induction on $L$. Closure under addition therefore gives $AP-I_B\in\Psi^{-L}(B,B)$ for every $L\geq1$. The sign is checked already at $L=1$, when the finite remainder is $E$. No limit of operator identities is taken.

source.place: §3.B, paragraph following Definition 3.8, printed p.14: the asymptotic expansion is an inverse modulo regular operators

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-pseudodifferential-residual-kernel] to the continuous real-linear distributional map $T=AP-I_B$ with $E=F=B$. It supplies a real smooth kernel $K(x,y):B_y\to B_x$ such that $AP-I_B=R_K$ on every distribution, with the fixed volume form and duality convention. Evaluating this equality at any $u\in\mathcal D\prime(B)$ yields $A(Pu)=u+R_Ku$ in $\mathcal D\prime(B)$, with no regularity assumption on $u$.

source.place: §3.B, regular-kernel paragraph after Proposition 3.6, printed p.13, applied to the inverse constructed on p.14
